cultural_notes: the Makah Tribe has lived at the northwestern tip of the Olympic Peninsula for thousands of years; five historic villages (Waatch, Sooes, Deah/Neah Bay, Ozette, Bahaada) with roughly 1,500 members in and around Neah Bay today (source: Makah Tribal Info + history, makah.com)

western red cedar is central to Makah life -- longhouses, ocean canoes, bark clothing; the Makah Cultural and Research Center displays Ozette artifacts (source: Makah, en.wikipedia.org; content.lib.washington.edu)
Makah Days each August commemorates Makah culture and the anniversary of US citizenship (source: makah.com/attractions/makah-days)

SOVEREIGNTY GUARDRAIL: cedar is a cultural cue for photography only, never an ingredient; the salmon cross-promo is a PROPOSAL requiring Makah consent (consent_status 'maybe'); do NOT imply or fabricate any Makah endorsement, and route any activation through the Tribe. This record documents public cultural context only -- it does not authorize use of Makah imagery, language, or fishery without Tribal agreement
